A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CB-LLM research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–B are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, human-evaluation, generation, concept-unlearning, and toxicity-steering results in Sections 3–4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds backbone comparisons in Tables 7 and 12 and another toxicity-steering example.

M1.justification: The five-step classification pipeline and the generation architecture with adversarial disentanglement retain the same procedures and objectives. Naming the cosine-cubed similarity and specifying layer dimensions clarify the method; they do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions use SST2, YelpP, AGnews, DBpedia, and the ToxicDPOqa/toxic-chat toxicity setting. Additional backbones and an illustrative toxicity prompt do not introduce a distinct dataset, task, or evaluation environment.

E2.justification: Tables 7 and 12 add evaluated fine-tuned Gemma2-2B, Llama2-13B, and Mistral-7B black-box comparators. These extend the existing black-box comparison strategy; the earlier TBM&C3M and backbone-specific comparisons remain.

E3.justification: Appendices A.1 and B.1 introduce Gemma2-2B classification and Llama2-13B/Mistral-7B generation configurations. Previously reported sample caps, metrics, and the 100-token steering procedure remain unchanged. These are additional model settings, not documented revisions to the original experiments.

E4.justification: Table 7 extends the sparse-final-layer comparison to Gemma2-2B, and Appendix B.4 adds a toxicity-steering case in Figure 16. Existing ACC/adversarial ablations and unlearning analyses are retained; Figure 15 redisplays the existing generation examples.

E5.justification: Both versions report three independent worker evaluations per human-study question. v2 adds no model-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical tests, including for its new backbone results.

E6.justification: Tables 7 and 12 substantially expand concrete results across three additional backbones, covering classification accuracy and generation accuracy, steerability, and perplexity. Table 5 also changes Llama3-based CB-LLM's DBpedia steerability from 0.58 to 0.76 without explaining the revision. Other main-table results and the existing GPT2 results are retained.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(9) retain their mathematical substance. Explicit layer dimensions and revised weight notation restate the existing architecture; no new theorem, proof, substantive assumption, or derivation appears.

C1.justification: The central claims remain scalable interpretable classification and generation, near-black-box performance, improved faithfulness, and controllable generation. v2 foregrounds safety and concept unlearning in the abstract and conclusion, but these applications and claims were already present in v1.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 newly states that supplied generation concept labels are unnecessary because ACS could provide concept scores. This expands the stated applicability beyond the documented label-supervised experiments, without reporting a corresponding evaluation. The principal result interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 3.1 newly identifies the similarity function as cosine cubed, and Section 4.1 explicitly describes generation-layer dimensions. Existing prompting instructions, regularization constants, timing results, and code access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Classification with Conceptual Safeguards, Discover-then-Name, and VLG-CBM. Section 2 briefly discusses VLG-CBM's faithfulness and Number of Effective Concepts metric. The overall positioning against existing text bottleneck models remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract and portions of the introduction, expands the generation-module explanation, and standardizes CB-LLMs terminology. It moves the MTurk appendix from A.1 to A.7, while retaining the main classification-then-generation organization.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 3 receive visual revisions, and Figure 15 is redrawn around the same generated examples. Tables 7 and 12 and Figure 16 are added. Most existing appendix displays are retained with relocation, renumbering, or sizing changes.

improvement.justification: The additional backbone comparisons provide useful evidence of portability beyond v1's tested models, while the explicit similarity choice and revised diagrams improve clarity. The gains are limited by sparse documentation and absent uncertainty estimates for the added experiments. The unexplained DBpedia score revision does not itself establish a performance improvement.
